title: Bai with Sa-um (Fermented Pork Fat)
steps: Boil seasonal vegetables and bamboo shoot with a little sa-um and salt.
Add local herbs and chilli towards the end. Simmer into a light, flavourful stew.
Serve with steamed rice – the quintessential Mizo everyday dish.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (pumpkin leaves, beans, spinach, etc.)
Bamboo shoot, sa-um (fermented pork fat), chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Bai with fermented pork fat – the most traditional version.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Sa-um gives the distinctive deep, savoury flavour.

title: Bai with Bekang (Vegetarian)
steps: Boil seasonal vegetables and bamboo shoot with bekang and salt.
Add local herbs and chilli towards the end. Simmer into a light, flavourful stew.
Serve with steamed rice – a vegetarian version of the quintessential Mizo dish.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (pumpkin leaves, beans, spinach, etc.)
Bamboo shoot, bekang (fermented soybean), chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of Bai using fermented soybean.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Bekang gives a unique fermented depth without meat.

title: Sawhchiar
steps: Cook rice and meat together with onion, ginger, garlic and herbs, adding enough water for a soft, porridge-like consistency.
Simmer until the rice breaks down and the flavours meld.
Serve hot – a comforting rice-and-meat porridge.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, ginger, garlic, local herbs, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mizo-style congee – warming and filling.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Anthur (roselle) leaves can be added for a tangy note.

title: Chhum Han
steps: Steam or boil the vegetables with ginger and a little chilli until just tender.
Season lightly with salt. Serve as a clean, simple side with rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Oil-free steamed vegetables – highlights natural flavours.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A light and healthy accompaniment.

title: Vawksa Rep
steps: Cook the smoked pork until tender. Add bamboo shoot, chilli and herbs.
Simmer so the smoky meat and tangy bamboo shoot flavours combine.
Serve with rice – one of the most loved Mizo dishes.

fullIngredients.name: Bamboo shoot, green chilli, local herbs

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Smoking the pork over wood is traditional and essential for authentic taste.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Bamboo shoot cuts the richness.

title: Vegetable Bai
steps: Boil the vegetables with bekang, onion, garlic, chilli and salt into a light stew.
Finish with fresh local herbs. Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Bekang (fermented soybean), onion, garlic, local herbs, chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of the classic Bai with added onion and garlic for flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple and nutritious.

title: Hmarcha Rawt
steps: Crush or pound fresh chillies with salt and garlic (and tomato if desired) into a coarse, fiery chutney.
Serve as the essential spicy accompaniment to any Mizo meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The classic Mizo chilli chutney – tangy, spicy and addictive.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Adjust heat to preference.

title: Smoked Pork with Mustard Leaves
steps: Cook the pork until tender. Add mustard leaves and continue cooking until the greens wilt and the flavours blend.
Season simply. Serve with rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mustard leaves add a distinctive peppery note to the rich pork.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A classic combination.

title: Sanpiau
steps: Prepare a soft rice porridge. Top with layers of crispy fried rice wafers, chilli chutney, fried chicken or fish, onion and coriander.
Eat mixed together – a popular street-food style dish.

fullIngredients.name: Fried chicken or fish, chilli chutney, crispy rice wafers, onion, coriander

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Street-food favourite in Aizawl and beyond.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The contrast of soft porridge and crunchy toppings is key.

title: Chhangban
steps: Soak and grind sticky rice into a paste or use whole grains. Steam or cook into dense rice cakes or bread-like pieces.
Eat plain, with jaggery, or as a snack with tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional sticky-rice snack – portable and filling.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often carried to the fields.

title: Bekang
steps: Bekang is traditionally prepared by fermenting cooked soybeans. Once ready, it can be eaten as is or lightly seasoned.
Use as a side, snack, or flavouring agent in Bai and other dishes.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mizo fermented soybean – similar to Japanese natto in concept.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pungent and protein-rich.

title: Bamboo Shoot Stir-fry
steps: Slice bamboo shoot and stir-fry briefly with onion, garlic, chilli, herbs and a touch of oil.
Season with salt. Serve as a crisp side with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, garlic, local herbs, green chilli, salt, a little oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Highlights the fresh, crunchy texture of young bamboo shoot.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal seasoning preserves the natural taste.

title: Simple Dal
steps: Boil the lentils with onion, garlic and salt until soft. Keep the consistency light.
Optionally temper with a little chilli or herbs. Serve with rice as a simple side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, garlic, salt, optional chilli or local herbs

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Mizos use dal more sparingly than in mainland India; it is a supporting dish.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Kept mild to complement other flavours.
